home.intro: LIREI is a multidisciplinary team of researchers, members of the Hydrogen Research Institute (IRH) at the Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières. Since 1999, we have been working to optimize energy use in buildings and vehicles, with a particular interest in hydrogen and renewable energy.

lab.title: The laboratory
lab.lead: A centre of innovation and exploration at the heart of the Hydrogen Research Institute, where a multidisciplinary team designs tomorrow's intelligent energy solutions.
lab.intro1: LIREI brings together professors, research professionals and graduate students around a shared mission: proposing solutions for intelligent energy management, from the power grid to buildings and vehicles. Our work combines optimization, machine learning, modeling and experimentation on real-world data.
lab.history1: The Hydrogen Research Institute (IRH) at UQTR was publicly inaugurated in 1996. Three years later, in 1999, LIREI was created as a multidisciplinary team within the Institute, with the mission of proposing solutions to manage energy intelligently.
lab.history2: Today, the laboratory pursues its activities in Trois-Rivières and is preparing to move into the new research facilities of UQTR's Pellerin-Marmen building.
lab.programsLead: Our activities are organized around three major programs that structure the laboratory's doctoral projects and collaborations.

lab.infraLead: LIREI operates an instrumented apartment, a storage bench, a computing cluster and simulation platforms, which together let its work be validated all the way from model to real conditions.

apartment.title: Smart apartment
apartment.desc: A fully instrumented dwelling at the Hydrogen Research Institute, where demand management strategies meet real use: heating and cooling driven by a Delta Controls controller over BACnet, water heater, appliances, EV charging stations and circuit-by-circuit consumption metering. Using an open building automation protocol means strategies can be tested on the same equipment found in commercial buildings. This is where the laboratory's algorithms meet occupant behaviour.

storage.title: Storage and conversion bench
storage.desc: A Victron Energy Quattro 5,000 VA 48 V inverter-charger — pure sine wave, 70 A charger, two AC inputs with an integrated transfer switch — coupled to two Fortress Power eFlex 5.4 kWh batteries, 10.8 kWh of lithium iron phosphate with closed-loop communication between the batteries and the inverter. The two inputs allow switching between grid, generator and islanded operation: self-consumption, peak shaving, grid support and isolated microgrid.

growth.title: Instrumented growth chamber
growth.desc: A climate-controlled growth enclosure, instrumented for temperature and humidity and supervised through an open home-automation platform that continuously historises the measurements. It offers a small scale, freely controllable, on which to test predictive control and greenhouse energy management strategies before transposing them to real conditions.

edge.title: Edge computing cluster
edge.desc: A thirteen-node cluster — eleven Raspberry Pi 4 boards and two x86 servers — under Kubernetes, carrying acquisition and control close to the equipment: wireless sensors, message broker, local historian and execution of control policies. Its size makes it a platform for studying distributed agent deployment and the division of work between edge and cloud.

cluster.title: Computing cluster
cluster.desc: Four Dell PowerEdge R740xd servers totalling 384 execution threads, close to 4 TB of memory and eight NVIDIA Tesla P40 accelerators (192 GB of GPU memory), under Kubernetes with distributed storage. The cluster hosts model training, simulation campaigns and the laboratory's data platforms.

simulation.title: Simulation and digital twins
simulation.desc: Co-simulation of distribution and communication networks, network digital twins and physics-based greenhouse simulators, to test transactive mechanisms and control strategies at a scale unreachable in the laboratory.

datasets.title: Data and historian
datasets.desc: Measurements from the apartment and the test benches — consumption, charging, occupancy, climate — are stored as time series and feed modelling, forecasting and machine learning.

lab.env1: The laboratory offers an inclusive and innovative environment that fosters interdisciplinary collaboration, mentorship and scientific dissemination. Graduate students benefit from supervision conducive to professional development and publication.
lab.env2: LIREI's work attracts strong industrial interest in Quebec: our network of partners is the main source of project funding.
lab.ctaText: LIREI is always looking for motivated graduate students interested in intelligent energy management.
lab.timelineLead: Thirty years of research, reconstructed from the lab's publications, defended theses and major agreements.

timeline.title: The IRH is inaugurated
timeline.desc: UQTR's Hydrogen Research Institute is publicly inaugurated.

timeline.title: LIREI is founded
timeline.desc: The laboratory is created as a multidisciplinary team within the IRH, with the mission of proposing solutions to manage energy intelligently.

timeline.title: Hydrogen and remote sites
timeline.desc: Early work centres on standalone renewable systems coupled with hydrogen: electrolyzers, fuel cells and storage for remote sites. More than half the period's publications deal with hydrogen.

timeline.title: The lab's first doctorate
timeline.desc: Alben Cardenas Gonzalez defends a thesis on integrating decentralized energy sources into the local grid. He is now a professor at UQTR.

timeline.title: Transport electrification
timeline.desc: Energy management for electric and fuel-cell vehicles joins the agenda, accounting for over a third of the period's publications.

timeline.title: An experimental apartment
timeline.desc: The lab commissions an instrumented apartment — communicating thermostats and smart loads — to test, model and optimize residential energy under real conditions.

timeline.title: The turn to residential buildings
timeline.desc: Demand forecasting, thermal storage, non-intrusive load monitoring and occupant-behaviour modelling become the core of the work: residential rises to 41% of publications.

timeline.title: First Hydro-Québec Research Chair
timeline.desc: Creation of the Hydro-Québec Research Chair on Transactive Management of Residential Power and Energy Demand, held by Professor Kodjo Agbossou.

timeline.title: Alliance program 2023-2028
timeline.desc: Launch of the research program on transactive flexibility management with Hydro-Québec's LTE/IREQ and Polytechnique Montréal, backed by NSERC, Mitacs and four industrial partners.

timeline.title: A second Chair, broader in scope
timeline.desc: The chair is renewed for five years ($3.28M) and becomes the Hydro-Québec Research Chair on Transactive Management of Electrical Energy. It adopts an open intellectual-property approach: results, including code, are released freely.

timeline.title: Transactive energy and flexibility markets
timeline.desc: Market mechanisms, multi-agent coordination and machine learning now dominate — 35% of recent publications address transactive energy and markets — extending to greenhouses and remote communities.

lab.pavillonLead: LIREI will move part of its activities into UQTR’s new research building on green and sustainable technologies, in downtown Trois-Rivières.
lab.pavillonBody: The building offers 4,200 m² over four floors and a basement, and will house more than fifteen research laboratories across four axes: energy, food, environment and sustainable development. It is itself an object of study: geothermal energy, photovoltaic panels, biofactories and rooftop urban greenhouses.
lab.pavillonBody2: Begun in March 2024, construction reached provisional handover in spring 2026, with occupancy planned for the fall. The spaces allocated to the laboratory will be detailed here once the fit-out is complete.

research.title: Research
research.lead: LIREI structures its work around three major research programs, expressed through doctoral projects and collaborations, and spanning a broad range of areas of expertise.

smartgrids.title: Smart grids and simulation platforms
smartgrids.desc: Design and simulation of smart power grids that use computing to better manage consumption and energy exchanges between suppliers and consumers. Two-level coordination and control of distributed systems.

residential.title: Residential energy management
residential.desc: Energy management systems for residential buildings: demand response, thermal storage, consumption monitoring and occupant comfort.
residential.tags: demand response, thermal storage, energy efficiency

ml.title: Machine learning and consumption monitoring
ml.desc: Application of machine learning to non-intrusive load monitoring, occupancy detection and stochastic modeling of electrical loads.
ml.tags: machine learning, occupancy detection, stochastic modeling

hydrogen.title: Hydrogen and fuel cells
hydrogen.desc: Integration of hydrogen and fuel cells into energy systems, in synergy with renewable energy and the work of the Hydrogen Research Institute.

flexibility.title: Transactive markets and mechanisms
flexibility.desc: Transactive energy mechanisms and local flexibility markets: convex optimization, economic analysis, equity and multi-agent coordination of distributed energy resources.
flexibility.tags: transactive energy, convex optimization, flexibility markets, multi-agent

ev.title: Electric vehicles and smart mobility
ev.desc: Optimization of energy use in electric and hydrogen vehicles, and integration of vehicles into the grid as flexibility providers.
ev.tags: electric vehicles, smart charging, sustainable mobility

flex.title: Transactive management architecture
flex.caption: The program's three levels: customers offer their flexibility, aggregators pool it, and the market and grid operator value it under physical constraints.
flex.alt: Three-level diagram: residential customers and their flexible resources offer flexibility to aggregators, which pool it and present it to the local flexibility market and the grid operator; prices and setpoints flow back down to the customers.

serres.title: Predictive control loop of a greenhouse
serres.caption: Forecasts and the crop model feed a controller robust to uncertainty; measurements close the loop and also drive anomaly diagnosis.
serres.alt: Closed loop: weather forecasts and the crop model feed a robust predictive controller, which drives the greenhouse's heating, ventilation and lighting; climate and growth measurements return to the controller and feed anomaly detection.

comm.title: Two-level management of an isolated microgrid
comm.caption: The CRSNG strand's architecture: day-ahead planning sets safe power limits; within them, agents learn to coordinate resources in real time.
comm.alt: Two-level architecture: planning through dynamic operational envelopes, computed by stochastic optimization over a 24-hour horizon, sets power limits; below, reinforcement-learning agents coordinate wind, solar, hybrid storage and residential loads in real time, which report their states.

opportunities.title: Opportunities
opportunities.lead: Coming to study and work at LIREI: the environment, the city, and what awaits you during and after.
opportunities.openLead: Specific positions, attached to a funded project.
opportunities.openNone: No specific position is open at the moment. The spontaneous applications below remain welcome.
opportunities.ongoingLead: The kinds of position the laboratory regularly hosts. Funding depends on current grants.
opportunities.howLead: One way in, whatever the posting: the contact form. It delivers your file to the laboratory's mailbox.
opportunities.step1Title: Choose the program and the level
opportunities.step1Desc: Read the three research programs and find the one your work fits. An application that names a specific program is handled faster than a general one.
opportunities.step2Desc: A CV in PDF, your transcripts, and a one-page letter saying what you want to study and why here. Publications, code repositories or earlier theses help.
opportunities.step3Desc: Pick the subject matching the position and attach your CV. The form accepts PDF, DOC and DOCX files up to 3.5 MB.
opportunities.step4Desc: Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis. If your profile matches a current or upcoming project, a faculty member will write back to arrange a conversation.
opportunities.money1: Funding depends on current grants and on the program you are applying to. Doctoral projects attached to a funded program usually come with a scholarship; at other levels, support varies with the funds available when you apply.
opportunities.money2: Applications backed by an external scholarship application are particularly welcome — NSERC, the Fonds de recherche du Québec and the Mitacs programs, all of which the laboratory already works with. We are glad to support such applications.
opportunities.ediText: LIREI brings together people from four continents and is committed to an open and respectful research environment. The laboratory subscribes to the equity, diversity and inclusion policies of Université du Québec à Trois-Rivières, which govern recruitment and student supervision.
opportunities.offerCityDesc: A French-speaking university of the Université du Québec network, halfway between Montreal and Quebec City on the St. Lawrence. A city on a human scale, where campus, housing and daily life sit close together rather than an hour apart — and where the laboratory will soon move into the new downtown research building.
opportunities.offerPeopleDesc: The laboratory brings together people from West Africa, Latin America, North Africa, the Middle East, Europe and Quebec, and sustains working ties with fifteen universities across four continents. Research is published in English; university life runs in French, and UQTR supports learning the language.
opportunities.offerAfterDesc: Our graduates continue in research — several have returned to the laboratory as postdoctoral fellows — or join industry and partner research centres, among them Hydro-Québec's LTE. One is now a professor at UQTR. Because projects run with industrial partners, those connections exist well before the thesis is finished.
opportunities.offerTrainingDesc: More than half the publication catalogue is conference papers: students present their own work, in Canada and abroad. The laboratory supports that participation, along with continuing training — summer schools, workshops and methodological development.
